messages:
mateo: Heads-up — nightly samplebench flagged a tail-latency bump on Ampere for candidate kernels. Seqlen sweep shows a sharp regression around 1k-2k tokens.

samira: ugh, saw that in the dashboard. Is it consistent across runs? :thinking_face:

mateo: Mostly. CI run 2024-11-09_03:12 had the worst; subsequent reruns are intermittent. I attached the microprofiler traces to the build artifacts.

perf-ci-bot: [CI] samplebench-nightly #402 finished — summary: 7/120 microbench configs failed threshold (latency +18% median, tail +35%). Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/samplebench/402/

jordan: Can you paste the failing config snippet? especially arch+seq sizes.

mateo: Sure — from the harness: ```yaml
arch: ampere_a100
model: gpt-small-fp16
batching: auto
seq_lengths: [32,128,512,1024,1536,2048]
kv_policy: prefix_cache
kernel_candidates: [kblk_v2, kblk_v1, matmul_opt]
```

alisha: Interesting that kblk_v2 gets picked at 1024/1536 and that's where latency spikes. kblk_v1 is slightly slower in throughput but has better memory locality for midseq.

mateo: Exactly. The autotuner's scoring pushed kblk_v2 because of peak throughput on synthetic long sequences, but the CI workload mixes shorter warmups and cache misses so cold-KV behavior dominates.

ryan: Do we have the perf counters? I suspect thrash in L2 due to the kernel's tiling for mid seqlens.

mateo: Perf counters attached. From the trace: L2 misses +42% and GPU DRAM reads +30% when kblk_v2 was selected at 1024. Also observed KV cache churn — kv-hit drops from 0.92 -> 0.64 in that window.

samira: So two issues: kernel micro-ops causing memory amplification + KV cache policy not handling the mixed seq distribution. What if we bias autotune to prefer lower working-set kernels for seq<2048?

jordan: We can add an architecture-aware heuristic: if arch==ampere && seq in [512,1536] prefer kblk_v1 unless demonstrable end-to-end p99 improvement. Short-term patch: add a cost penalizer in harness scoring.

alisha: Agreed. Add a multiplicative penalty on estimated DRAM bytes for candidate kernels. That should discourage kblk_v2 for mixed workloads.

mateo: I'll open a small PR to the harness scoring heuristics. Plan: (1) add dram_estimate factor, (2) re-run samplebench-nightly in canary mode, (3) if green promote. ETA a few hours.

perf-ci-bot: [ACTION] Created ticket PERF-1218: "autotune: penalize kernels with high DRAM estimate for midseq on Ampere" — https://board.redwood/perf/1218

ryan: Also suggest adding a microprobe targeting KV cache eviction behavior: run a hot-prefix pattern vs random access to measure kv-hit sensitivity per kernel. We can include as a tiny harness case.

samira: Good call. If we can quantify kv-hit delta per kernel we can fold that into the score. Mateo, can you include that microprobe in the canary sweep?

mateo: Yep. I'll add a microprobe config: ```json
{
 "probe_name": "kv_eviction_midseq",
 "pattern": "prefix-heavy",
 "seq": 1024,
 "ramp": 2000
}
```

alisha: One more ask — record the chosen kernel path in the CI metadata (we currently only store final perf). That will help correlate kernel picks with regressions faster.

mateo: Good call, adding kernel_choice to artifacts metadata.

jordan: If the canary shows improvement, let's push a gating rule to prevent kblk_v2 from being auto-selected for Ampere in the mixed workload pool until we rebenchmark with a larger kv-cache config.

mateo: Sounds good. I'll keep this thread updated with run links. Starting the canary now.

perf-ci-bot: [CI] samplebench-canary #403 queued on ampere-01. Expect ~45m for full sweep.

samira: thanks — will follow logs. :rocket:
